Description: Record every delivered batch and always dispense from the valid batch that expires first.
Warn staff about batches nearing expiry early enough to act on them.
Turn low stock into purchase orders that suppliers can see once they are dispatched.
Give staff a clear view of stock and give managers proof that the system performs.
As a pharmacy technician, I want to register each delivery with its batch number, expiry date and quantity, so that every pack on the shelf can be traced.
As a pharmacist, I want the system to pick the valid batch with the earliest expiry date when I dispense, so that older stock leaves the shelf first.

Summary: Story 1.3: Reject expired batch at checkout
Description: As a cashier, I want an expired batch to be rejected at checkout and the next valid batch suggested, so that I never sell out-of-date medicine.
As a pharmacy manager, I want a daily list of batches expiring within 30 days, so that I can return or discount them in time.
As a pharmacist, I want near-expiry alerts shown on my dashboard when I log in, so that I notice them without running a report.

Summary: Story 3.1: Set minimum stock per medicine
Description: As a pharmacy manager, I want to set a minimum stock level for each medicine, so that the system knows when to reorder.

Summary: Story 3.2: Draft purchase order at low stock
Description: As a pharmacy manager, I want a draft purchase order created when stock falls below its minimum, so that shortages are prevented without manual checks.
As a supplier, I want to see the purchase orders dispatched to me, so that I can prepare the delivery.
As a pharmacy staff member, I want one screen showing the quantity, expiry date and status of every batch, so that I can answer stock questions quickly.
As a pharmacy manager, I want a report on response times and uptime, so that I can confirm the system copes with busy hours.
